result.summary: Hardens legacy wallet migration to SQLite and descriptor formats against mid-process failures and unexpected filesystem exceptions. MigrateToSQLite now stages the new SQLite database in a temporary directory and only deletes the original BerkeleyDB file after the new database is fully written. Exceptions during sub-wallet creation and migration are caught to enable graceful errors and automated restoration of the original wallet from backup without manual intervention.
result.problem: During legacy wallet migration, MigrateToSQLite previously deleted the original BerkeleyDB file before verifying that the SQLite database could be fully written, forcing users to manually recover from backups if writing failed. In addition, encountering read-only directories or throwing exceptions during descriptor creation crashed the migration mid-flight and skipped failure cleanup routines.
evidence: PR description: 'The goal of the PR is to handle failures in a controlled way. Just so the process can automatically restore the original wallet without requiring user manual intervention.'

Commit ba250143c4: 'This is not really the best because it removes the original db before making sure the sqlite one is fully built. If creation fails, the wallet ends up partly in sqlite format with legacy records, and the user has to restore from a backup manually.'
result.changed_since_previous: The core approach remains the same; added cross-filesystem migration handling using copy_file with error codes and associated functional test coverage.
result.card: This pull request hardens legacy-to-descriptor wallet migration against mid-process crashes and filesystem permission errors. It stages new SQLite databases in temporary directories before removing original BerkeleyDB files and wraps migration in exception handlers to ensure post-failure cleanup. Without this, migration failures could leave users with partially migrated databases requiring manual recovery from backups. It touches wallet storage logic and currently needs a rebase.

risk.why: A flaw in wallet file staging, copying, or cleanup during migration could delete or corrupt the original database file before the new SQLite wallet is fully written.
